rounds.text: The market is heavily discounting a fundamentally sound business whose price sits just 10% of the way up its 52-week range [E5] and trades at a P/E of 26.6x against a sector benchmark of 32.46x [E6]. Operating margins have expanded significantly, hitting 37% in the TTM compared to 27% three years earlier [E30], driven by robust sales growth of 14% over both the 3-year and trailing twelve-month periods [E16, E17]. Furthermore, the company is almost debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.01x [E38, E60], generated Rs 96 Cr in free cash flow [E36], and maintains a healthy dividend payout of 65.8% [E61]. A discounted cash flow model puts intrinsic value above the current market price of Rs 4,923 [E2, E45], creating an explicit margin of safety [E46] while a reverse DCF shows the stock only prices in 16.3% earnings growth against a base case expectation of 18.0% [E47]. Conceded: compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months dropped by -16% [E21], and institutional money flow shows a negative reading with foreign holdings decreasing [E42, E44].

Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 26.6x against a sector benchmark of 32.46x [E6], and free cash flow reached Rs 96 Cr in Mar 2026 [E36]. However, the bull's reliance on a 10% position in the 52-week range [E5] ignores severe technical deterioration, as the price sits below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E50], with a relative-strength rating of just 13 [E51] and a 12-month return of -25.3% [E52]. Conceded: TTM operating margins expanded to 37% [E30], but this profitability is suspect given that earnings include Rs 62.7 Cr of other income [E62], and TTM compounded profit growth actually collapsed by -16% [E21]. While the DCF and reverse DCF models project value [E45, E47], institutional confidence is fleeing through a negative money flow signal [E44] and foreign institutional holdings dropping to 6.90% [E42]. Finally, the rules-based screen score of 49 out of 100 [E63] and lagging market momentum [E51, E70] demonstrate that the low valuation reflects genuine underlying risks rather than an overlooked bargain.
